_comment: Hand corrections to the OCR pass, folded in by tools/build_coords.py.
Positions are pixels of .build/a19/drawing_full.png (6140 x 2155) for the
board and of .build/a19/sch1_full.png (6310 x 3855) for the sheet -- NOT of
the downscaled images the browser loads.
How this board read. The drawing gave 65 of 140 designators (46%), about
what A17 managed and for the same reason: most of what is missing is the
dense right-hand section, where the diode and resistor labels are 25 px of
rotated silkscreen packed four to the centimetre. The schematic read far
better -- 113 of 140, 81% -- because it is typeset rather than silkscreened.
Every one of the 65 board markers and every one of the 113 sheet markers was
rendered onto its source image and looked at. On the board 10 were wrong; on
the sheet 17 were, and 13 of those 17 were the two legend blocks in the
right-hand margin, exactly as references/pitfalls.md predicts. Everything the
reader missed and everything it got wrong is placed by hand below, measured
off a 50 px grid over the full-resolution image.
All 13 test points are hand-placed on both spaces as a matter of course. On
the board each box spans the signal name, the pad and the TP number together,
because the pad is a bare tick between the two pieces of text and a marker on
the text alone sends a probe to the wrong side of it.
_dropComment: H7 is a tubular rivet with no silkscreen designator. The reader put a marker
on it spanning a third of the board -- it had merged several unrelated reads
-- which also made a part that belongs in notOnDrawing look placed. That is
the A18 MP2 failure again, so it is dropped here and listed below.
Everything else the reader got wrong is replaced rather than dropped, since
a hand entry under 'board' already wins.
_dropSchematicComment: Seven reads on sheet 1 that are not this designator anywhere on the sheet.
C10 is the letter C of the Q4 bottom-view legend in the COMPONENT I.D. box.
M1 and M2 are rubber feet, H5/H6/H7 are a heat sink and two rivets and MP8
is a nut -- none of them has a schematic symbol at all; the reader found
them in 'MPSU10', 'MR850', '1N4002' and two P41 pin numbers.
Q3, Q9 and Q10 are dropped implicitly instead: their only read was the
caption of the TO-202 package legend, and each is re-placed by hand on its
own transistor, which is a better answer than dropping.
_notOnDrawingComment: 27 parts with no silkscreen designator on the locator drawing: two rubber
feet, two nylon ejectors, two grommets, two spacers, the TO-3 and TO-220
heat sinks and clips, the insulators, and every screw, nut and rivet. They
stay searchable in the parts list; counting them as unplaced would make the
coverage badge lie and send someone hunting for a washer that was never
drawn. Note that the two ejectors ARE drawn -- the ears at the top corners --
but they carry no designator, which is what this list is about.
_boardComment: Measured by eye off a 50 px grid over drawing_full.png and rendered back to
check. Ten of these correct a marker the reader placed somewhere else:
C2   was on C9's label at the far left of the board
C5   was on the '+5V' silkscreen beside TP12
C7   was on the CR25/CR27 outlines
C17  was on R9's resistor body
CR1  was on CR13's label -- a truncation misread, the A18 MP2 shape again
F1   was a box spanning Q9 and Q10
L5   was on an unlabelled outline below L3 in the left cluster
L7   was on the small outline beside C22, not on the choke that carries
the L7 silkscreen inside its own circle
R1   was in the middle of the blank centre panel, 3000 px from the part
TP4  was on TP11's label, at the opposite end of the board
The rest are parts the reader never found. Boxes are sized to the label:
110 x 48 for horizontal silkscreen, 48 x 110 for the rotated labels that
make up most of the right-hand section.

_schematicComment: Sixteen hand placements on sheet 1. Three are test points the reader could
only find in the legend table in the right-hand margin (TP1, TP10) or found
on the wrong net (TP5 landed on TP9's -12VUR flag, the TPS/TP5 confusion the
pitfalls file names). Three are transistors whose only read was the caption
of the TO-202 package legend -- 'Q3, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10' is a row of genuine
designators laid out in a grid, which is exactly the block that arrives in
the agreed tier looking trustworthy. U1 was read off the '100uF' of C15.
The rest are the seven chokes and two resistors the reader never found.

TP1.note: On the +75VUR flag. The reader had it in the test point legend table.

TP5.note: On the +35V flag. The reader had it on TP9's -12VUR flag.

TP10.note: On the -12V flag. The reader had it in the test point legend table.

U1.note: Inside the 7812 block. The reader had read it off C15's '100uF'.

L4.note: moved onto the L4 designator above its coil in the final review pass (had sat on blank space above)

Q3.note: On the transistor itself; the reader had it on the package legend caption.

_layersComment: Photo alignment: 23 landmark pairs, solved as a full projective fit.
src is board space (the locator drawing), dst is photo image space, and H
Thirteen of the pairs are the test point pads themselves -- flat plated
holes, nothing standing over them, and spread right across the board's
1.5 m of width in board space, which is what fixes the horizontal scale.
The other ten are silkscreen designators low on the board, chosen only
where the text is clear of any component body in BOTH images.
Nothing here is an ejector, a standoff, a mounting hole or the top of an
electrolytic: those stand proud of the board and show 15-20 px of parallax
against flat artwork. Nor is anything taken from a part whose body covers
its own silkscreen in the photograph -- the four fuses and C5, C7 and C17
were tried and dropped for exactly that reason. Their printed designators
sit under or beside the component in the photo and inside the outline on
the drawing, which produced 50-130 px of apparent disagreement that is not
Residuals against the 23 pairs: median 5.5 px, p90 16 px, worst 17 px, on
a 5671 x 2182 photograph -- about a tenth of a marker's width. That is the
accuracy of reading a landmark by eye rather than a limit of the fit.
_sheetsComment: The zone grid of sheet 1, measured off the printed frame: columns 8 to 1
left to right and rows D to A top to bottom, with 'frame' the inner border
in normalised sheet coordinates. Zone labels for every placement are derived
